answer.evidence: The seat is an ellipse. Its width profile runs 6, 8, 10, 10, 8, 6 over rows 6-11, widening and then narrowing again. The light lilac rows 7-8 are the seat top, and the darker rows 9-10 with the dark outline on row 11 are the cushion's front edge and shadow. Below it a narrow stem (rows 12-13, width 4) and a wider base (rows 14-15, width 8) form the front support. The seat surface is seen from above and the front face is 3 or more rows, so this reads as three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny purple stool with only 7 distinct colours in total. The seat shows a highlight, a mid tone and a dark tone, and the base and legs are a flat dark shape. The dark edge pixels are only 4% neutral, so the outline is tinted (a dark purple) rather than near-black. That part is acceptable. The piece is much smaller than the references and carries little texture: no grain, no dots, no per-part shading on the stem or legs. Visible tones per tile cannot be measured (0), so I judged by eye. Next to the bench (14 colours), the lamp (14) and the well (38), the candidate has about half the colours of the simplest references and looks thinner and flatter. Its shading is shallow at about 3 steps against the 5-6 steps of the references. A careful artist would not accept it next to them without it looking like a flat sticker.
